title: Does the washed-out layered CIPS population reach a steady birth-death balance, and can it then carry a heritable trait?
summary: In 20261026T1856-c44-cips-chemostat-two-seeds a random whole-body washout every 800-1100 t keeps the layered CIPS condensates dividing past the box-fill limit (generation 4-5), but births replace only 40-60% of removals and the population drifts from 15-16 to 9-12 bodies by t=30000. Two follow-ups. (1) Steady state: wash_T 1500 and 2500 to t=60000 on seeds 0-2 (192^2, ~70 min each at 2 threads; or 128^2 with Lsc=2 to save time), report births vs removals per 5000 t and whether the body count plateaus. (2) If it plateaus, the chemostat is a selection arena: give the enzyme two variants (e.g. two enzymes e1, e2 with different chi or kc, each drifting up the shared product) and ask whether the faster-dividing variant takes over under washout while a neutral twin (identical variants) drifts, the L7 test.
experiment: WORLD_P {"wash_T":1500,"wash_t0":12000,"noise":0.03} and {"wash_T":2500,...} with research/alife/collective/contrib/20261026T1819-c44-cips-chemostat-sighting/world.py, labkit --frames 600 (t=60000), seeds 0-2; count persistent splits and removals (s['wash_log']) per 5000 t.
